rows.name: LOGNAME

problems.statement: `bin/dice` then keeps its socket, state and log files in `/tmp/dice-<name>` by default.
problems.code_says: `/tmp/dice-<name>` is the runtime directory only when the host configuration is not `mode: shared`. In shared mode the directory is the parent of the configured socket or `/run/dice`. The daemon commands stop with an error unless the host configuration says `mode: shared`, so a running daemon never keeps its files in `/tmp/dice-<name>` by default.

problems.statement: `bin/dice`, `bin/slice`, `bin/dice_lsf_view.py`, through the Python function `getpass.getuser()` (the Tron cell says "Reads and sets", and no cell names the set)
problems.code_says: In shared mode the Dice daemon sets LOGNAME to the login name of the submitting user in the environment of the command of a submission, when the submitted environment has no LOGNAME.

Not a code fact. POSIX defines LOGNAME as a login variable in the Base Definitions (chapter 8.3, Other Environment Variables). It is not in the variable list of the POSIX shell. The rows `TERM` and `TMPDIR` of the same chapter use `POSIX`.
problems.site: external: POSIX.1-2017 XBD 8.3; document rows TERM and TMPDIR in table 7.1

problems.statement: `bin/dice_lsf_view.py` compares the name with the owner of an LSF job and warns when they differ.
problems.code_says: The comparison and the warning are in cancel_job(), which then cancels the job. The warning appears only on a cancel.

cells.Where: `bin/dice`, `bin/slice` and `bin/dice_lsf_view.py` read it through the Python function `getpass.getuser()`. On a shared host, the Dice daemon in `bin/dice` sets it to the login name of the submitter for a submission that lacks it.
cells.What Tron does with it: `getpass.getuser()` checks it first. On a legacy host, the default runtime directory of `bin/dice` is `/tmp/dice-<name>`. Before it cancels an LSF job, `bin/dice_lsf_view.py` compares the name with the owner of the job and warns when they differ.

evidence: bin/dice:118 - _TMP_DIR_DEFAULT = /tmp/dice-<getpass.getuser()>
bin/dice:405-419 - runtime_dir() returns _TMP_DIR_DEFAULT only outside shared mode; shared mode returns the socket parent or /run/dice
bin/dice:422-444 - socket, state, log and lock paths are below runtime_dir() unless a DICE_* path variable replaces them
bin/dice:342-350, 4349-4366, 4384-4385 - the daemon commands raise `shared Dice is not enabled on this host` unless the host configuration is shared
bin/dice:3629-3653 - in shared mode the daemon runs env.setdefault("LOGNAME", pw.pw_name) with the passwd entry of the submitter uid
bin/dice_lsf_view.py:1224-1252 - cancel_job() takes the requester from getpass.getuser(), prints a warning when the job owner differs or is unknown, then cancels

unresolved: TEMP, TMP - whether the rows should also name the indirect readers. Python `tempfile` (for example bin/dice-lsf-runner:433, bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py:285) and `std::filesystem::temp_directory_path()` in the test programs (for example t/fuse_test_env.hpp:31) read TMPDIR first and then TMP and TEMP. notes: All 12 rows are in table 7.1, which has no For column. Verdicts grade facts only. Six rows were changed. LC_ALL: the Where cell now starts with the required text `No reader in Tron.`. LD_LIBRARY_PATH, OSTYPE, PATH, PWD: the file counts are replaced with `and other files`. In OSTYPE and PATH the doubled list of program names and file paths is reduced to the file paths. In PATH the names `rinzler` and `runtron` now have backticks, and the sentence about `popen` says that the child shell inherits the variable. LOGNAME: three fixes. The default directory `/tmp/dice-<name>` applies only on a legacy host, and the present text read as if a running Dice daemon keeps its files there. The Where cell now names the set in bin/dice:3650. Defined by is now `POSIX`, the same label as TERM and TMPDIR. TEMP, TMP: `worker server` is now `FPGA server`, as the glossary finding proposed and as the header of bin/dice-lsf-runner confirms. The vague word `unusable` is replaced with the test that the code applies. The PATH finding about file counts is confirmed and applied. Not changed, for the editor of the other rows: the TMPDIR row still says `an unusable value`, and the USERNAME row describes the same default directory without the legacy-host condition. PS1: the hook changes the prompt only when `id -un` prints a name. The `__NIX_USERNAME` row already states that case, so the PS1 row is left as it is. TERM: bin/bsub-build passes `dumb` when TERM is unset or empty. The row leaves that out, and a reader does not act differently, so the row is left as it is. The checkout holds a staged copy of README.env-vars.md. Every search excluded it.
